Architecture for visitors

Engine Overview

Abyssal Engine combines an editor shell, WebGPU renderer, project system, asset registry, and modular gameplay framework.

Project Model

A project is the durable workspace and home for all authored content.

Project
  ├── assets/
  │   ├── meshes/
  │   ├── materials/
  │   └── fragments/
  ├── scenes/
  └── recipes/

Friendly names are used in the editor. Stable qualified IDs ensure reliable references between assets.

MeshAsset

Geometry metadata from built-in base meshes or imported OBJ files.

MaterialAsset

Appearance data for ReflectionLit materials (color, metallic, roughness, emissive, opacity).

FragmentAsset

Authored assembly of mesh nodes, empty pivots, transforms, and material references.

Construct

Runtime gameplay identity assembled from Fragments and configured with behavior.

Component

Reusable behavior attached to Actors (movement, combat, economy, etc.).

Renderer

WebGPU ReflectionLit pipeline with editor overlays for grid, gizmos, and picking.

Wings Assembler Workflow

MeshAsset → Add to Assembly
  → Build hierarchy (Root / Empty Pivot / Mesh)
  → Transform parts
  → Assign Materials
  → Save as FragmentAsset

Wings Assembler is the embedded modular authoring workspace using an isolated preview scene.

Guiding Philosophy

  • Build games, not demos.
  • Morninghollow is the proving ground.
  • Documentation is part of the architecture.
  • Modularity must solve real production problems.

Technology Stack

  • TypeScript + WebGPU
  • gl-matrix for math
  • Vite for builds

Tool Philosophy

Abyssal was not created to replace other engines. It cooperates with them. Blender remains the preferred bridge for broad content interchange.
